messages:
olivia (Marketing): Quick sync  need final status page line + an embargoed email variant and a one-line social blurb. Hold public post until we hit Monitoring. Can someone propose two short options? @ben @kevin

ben (SRE): Timeline: degraded requests starting 02:14 UTC, rollback at 02:37, systems stable 02:45. Root cause under investigation (autoscale misconfig). Monitoring in progress.

nina (Legal): Keep wording neutral on data. Use "no indication of customer data exposure" only after SRE confirms. Avoid words like "breach" or "loss".

kevin (Support): I'll compile impacted-account list and sample request IDs, ETA 20m. We need the email subject so we can prepare reply templates.

olivia (Marketing): Option 1 (clear):
```
Service degradation affecting a subset of API requests from 02:1402:45 UTC. We reverted a configuration change and services are healthy. Monitoring continues; a full incident report will follow within 72 hours.
```

Option 2 (concise):
```
Partial service degradation 02:1402:45 UTC. Rollback applied; systems healthy and under monitoring. Follow-up to come.
```

omar (Product): I prefer Option 1 for clarity. Also recommend adding a short FAQ line in the email about retrying failed requests.

olivia (Marketing): Plan: 1) Post Identified -> Monitoring progression on StatusPage using Option 1. 2) Send embargoed targeted email to impacted customers ~30m after CSV is uploaded. 3) Public social only after Monitoring. 4) Postmortem within 72 hours. Any objections?

ben (SRE): +1. Will confirm log check for data language before email send.

nina (Legal): +1 pending SRE confirmation line about data exposure phrasing.

kevin (Support): CSV will be uploaded to /shared/incidents/1801129999.csv in ~18m. I'll ping when ready.

statusbot: Incident INC-4932 updated by ben: state=identified, severity=low. (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4932)

olivia (Marketing): Great I'll draft the embargoed email subject/body and queue it for send once kevin uploads the CSV and ben confirms the wording. Thanks all.
